title: Laura Csuka (DPhil Student CS · Co-founder, Stealth Startup) — 'the best book on founding that I have ever encountered'
summary: Laura Csuka — DPhil student in Computer Science at Oxford, currently co-founding a stealth startup with Thomas Duffield — attends the OpenseedVC / Startup Leap event with 90% of the book already highlighted and dog-eared. Publishes her recap flagging Incorruptible's Epilogue as unusually load-bearing for a non-fiction closing chapter, and thanking Eric for 'the best book on founding that I have ever encountered.'
blockquote: I've been looking for a book like this for a long time, and I'm so grateful that Eric Ries wrote it just in time for it to arrive at the beginning of the company founding path Thomas Duffield and I are on. When I came to the event, I had already read about 90% of "Incorruptible: Why Good Companies Go Bad and How Great Companies Stay Great", so the version that I was lucky to get signed by Eric was already heavily bent and highlighted. I'm glad though that I was reminded not to stop short of the last part. Most of the time, last chapters in non-fiction books can be safely skipped because they tend to read like an afterthought. The Epilogue in Incorruptible couldn't be more different: it summarised the core message beautifully. Thank you Openseed VC for hosting the evening and thank you Eric Ries for writing the best book on founding that I have ever encountered.
